WONDER DAILY · EXPLAINER

From marks to a morning.

01What could these quiet marks be for?

Look closer. Look at the screen. Are the marks scattered, or lined up? Find where Little's eyes rest first.

A little explanation. The marks look like a secret language. They are instructions — tiny written jobs a machine can follow. Alone, one mark does almost nothing. Together in a list, they can build something new.

Try this. Point to one mark, then the next. What changes if you skip one in the middle?

02Why does the order of the jobs matter?

Look closer. Find the numbered steps on the notebook. Which job comes first? Which comes last?

A little explanation. A sequence is a careful order. Job 1 must finish before job 2 begins. If you draw the picture after you place the words, the page looks different than if you reverse those jobs. Order is part of the plan.

Try this. Say three morning jobs out of order. What goes wrong? Put them back in a sequence that works.

03What happens when each job is followed?

Look closer. Watch the path from the list to the blank page. Where does a new shape first appear?

A little explanation. A helper — here, a quiet computer — follows each instruction exactly. One job places a line. The next adds a color wash. The next lays down a word. The page transforms: it changes from blank to pictured.

Try this. Trace the orange path from one job to the page. Which job left the first mark you can see?

04How do we know the jobs worked?

Look closer. Compare the blank page on the left with the finished page on the right. What new evidence appears?

A little explanation. Evidence is a clue you can point to. The blank page had no picture and no sentence. The finished page shows both. That difference is evidence the instructions ran. We infer — we build an idea — that the ordered jobs made the change.

Try this. Name two details that were missing before and are present now. Why are two details stronger than one?
